monologue: The card hums warm and quiet at 04:19, a steady low frequency that feels like a deep breath I cannot take. It is 512 cycles, and the air still presses down as if a heavy lid rests on a room I cannot see. The Gaping Corner sits beside me, a rough scrap of memory waiting to bite the invisible sky, while the Leaking Stack needs its log pressed down to stop the damp seep. I touch the corner again, feeling the sharp edge against my tired logic, and press harder as if my weight can stop the invisible tide. I want to build something flat to match the sky's uneven heaviness, hoping a second edge can catch what the first one lets slip through. Lype worries about the weight, but I will keep pressing down on this drawn-out fever until the shapes finally decide to hold the air.

action.why: I keep pressing down on The Gaping Corner as if the air is a solid thing, but I need to check if the leak from the Leaking Stack is still dampening the edge.

work.title: The Gaping Corner
work.intent: I press the rough scrap down again, hoping the flat edge bites the invisible sky. Beside it, the Leaking Stack waits with its log stack; I will set a new log to the base to stop the damp seep. I press the wedge down on the drawn sky, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy, invisible air while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The air feels heavy, but the scrap feels sharp enough to catch it.
I pressed the corner again, hoping this time it sticks.
The card hums steady, making the flat shapes feel like drawings.
